column11: two shares multiplied. (1) The rectal share of colorectal cancer: 'rectal cancer now makes up nearly one-third (32%, up from 27% in the mid-2000s) of all colorectal cancer diagnoses' (American Cancer Society, Colorectal Cancer Facts and Figures 2026, cancer.org press release 'Rectal Cancer Incidence Rising After Decades of Decline', March 2026). (2) The locally advanced share: NCT05009069 enrols resectable rectal adenocarcinoma staged cT3 node-positive or cT4 any node, with metastatic disease excluded, which is regional-stage disease. SEER 21 (2016-2022) puts 37% of colorectal cancers at regional stage, against 34% localized, 23% distant and 6% unstaged (SEER Cancer Stat Facts, Percent of Cases by Stage). 0.32 x 0.37 = 0.1184
column12: the stage share is a proxy and it cuts both ways. SEER's 'regional' means spread to regional lymph nodes, which is the trial's cT3N+ arm, but the trial also admits cT4 node-negative disease that SEER would call localized, so this understates. Against that, not every locally advanced rectal patient completes neoadjuvant chemoradiotherapy and goes on to adjuvant immunotherapy. A narrower restriction the trial does not impose: it does not select on mismatch repair status

column11: a judgement for a checkpoint inhibitor added after neoadjuvant chemoradiotherapy in a setting where the standard of care is now total neoadjuvant therapy followed by surgery or watch-and-wait, and where the immunotherapy story in rectal cancer belongs to mismatch-repair-deficient disease and to dostarlimab rather than to an unselected PD-L1 antibody. Set against that, there is no approved immunotherapy at all for the mismatch-repair-proficient majority this study enrols

a judgement set below the published chain, on a stated result. NCT04661150 is completed, reported on 2023-05-08 and has posted results: pathological complete response in 38.1% of the atezolizumab arm (95% CI 18.1-61.6) against 14.3% of the trastuzumab plus XELOX control (95% CI 3.0-36.3), p=0.079 in 42 patients (ClinicalTrials.gov results section, read 2026-10-27). The point estimate is a near-trebling and the direction is right, but the difference did not reach conventional significance and three and a half years later no Phase 3 of atezolizumab in gastric cancer is registered. The published Oncology transitions from Phase 2 would give 0.246 x 0.477 x 0.920 = 0.108 (BIO/Informa Pharma Intelligence/QLS Advisors, 2011-2020, Figure 2 page 7); this is read below that because the Phase 2 gate has already been attempted and the programme has not advanced

The count: NICE's resource impact report for technology appraisal TA632, adjuvant trastuzumab emtansine (nice.org.uk/guidance/ta632/resources/resource-impact-report-pdf-8772971293), puts 840 people a year in England eligible for adjuvant T-DM1 with residual invasive disease after neoadjuvant taxane and HER2-targeted therapy, the KATHERINE population whose clinical-stage and preoperative therapy criteria ASTEFANIA repeats (clinicaltrials.gov API v2, NCT04873362, checked 2026-10-28). Scaled by population from the 56,286,961 residents of England at mid-2019 (Office for National Statistics) to the 340,110,988 US residents of 1 July 2024 (Census): 840 x 340,110,988 / 56,286,961 = 5,076 a year. 5,076 / 160,000 = 0.031725. Cross-check: 321,910 new US female breast cancers in 2026 (SEER Cancer Stat Facts) x 13.33% HER2-positive (HR-positive HER2-positive 9.40% and HR-negative HER2-positive 3.93%, SEER Cancer Stat Facts, Female Breast Cancer Subtypes, SEER 21, 2018 to 2022) = 42,908 HER2-positive cancers a year, of which 5,076 is 11.8%
column12: the weakest row in this file. The 840 was read from a search index of the NICE report and the England population is ONS's published mid-2019 estimate; neither nice.org.uk nor ons.gov.uk was reachable from this session. Per head it leans low, since US female breast cancer incidence runs above England's. It leans high for the years ahead: the FDA's 2026-05-15 approval of neoadjuvant trastuzumab deruxtecan on DESTINY-Breast11 (pathological complete response 67.3% against 56.3%) shrinks the residual-disease population by about a quarter where it is used. An annual count serves as the stock because adjuvant therapy runs 14 cycles every three weeks, about ten months

column11: a judgement, set low because the setting already has a new standard. On 2026-05-15 the FDA approved trastuzumab deruxtecan for HER2-positive breast cancer with residual invasive disease on DESTINY-Breast05, 1,635 patients, invasive disease-free survival hazard ratio 0.47 against T-DM1, 92.4% against 83.7% free of invasive disease at three years (as CURE and Epocrates reported the approval on 2026-05-15). ASTEFANIA adds atezolizumab to T-DM1, the arm DESTINY-Breast05 beat, so a positive readout still leaves the combination behind the new standard for most patients; its place is with patients who cannot take trastuzumab deruxtecan

a judgement set well below the published chain, and the row to argue with. The chain for an immuno-oncology Phase 3 is 0.490 Phase 3 to NDA/BLA (n=98) x 0.984 NDA/BLA to approval (n=62) = 0.482 (BIO/Informa/QLS 2011-2020, Figure 7 page 13; data/pos_transitions.csv). Both randomised tests of atezolizumab in HER2-positive breast cancer found in this session were negative: KATE2, this same T-DM1 combination in advanced disease, was unblinded for futility with progression-free survival hazard ratio 0.82 (95% CI 0.55 to 1.23, p=0.33) and more serious adverse events, 33% against 19% (Emens LA et al., Lancet Oncol 2020;21(10):1283-1295, doi:10.1016/S1470-2045(20)30465-4); IMpassion050, neoadjuvant, showed pathological complete response of 62.4% against 62.7% (Huober J et al., J Clin Oncol 2022;40(25):2946-2956, doi:10.1200/JCO.21.02772) and in its final analysis no significant event-free survival gain, hazard ratio 0.90 (95% CI 0.50 to 1.59) (Huober J et al., ESMO Open 2026, doi:10.1016/j.esmoop.2026.108541). And a US filing after a win would meet a standard that has moved to trastuzumab deruxtecan
